text:
Alex H: Quick postmortem follow-up —  FYI the rollout flag misconfig expanded to 40% vs intended 4% and that created the spike. Need a short remediation plan with clear owners + timelines. @Maria G can you take point on the auto-rollback work?

Maria G: Yep. I can own auto-rollback. Proposed approach: detection hook + automated flag flip + coordinated test harness. I can have a prototype PR by EOD Fri and a canary test next week. :+1:

Zayd R: Thanks. We should also add a blast-radius limiter for flag scopes (per-cluster / per-tenant caps). I can scope the limiter and add an enforce-timeout for flag changes. ETA: Wed next week for initial PR.

Jen S: I'll own the postmortem action tracker entry and the follow-up reminder cadence. I'll create recurring reminders (2w, 4w) to see if patterns recur. Also will add the rollout incident as a regression test in the release harness.

Alex H: Good. Two quick asks: (1) add an observable metric that triggers rollback (error_rate, latency p95, or increase in 5xx rate) and (2) make rollback idempotent and auditable. Maria — what metric do you want?

Maria G: Let's use a combined signal: service_error_rate > 0.015 sustained for 3m OR p95 latency increase > 40% vs baseline for 5m. I'll wire both into the detection pipeline. Also adding a dry-run mode for the early rollout to validate without flipping prod flags.

Zayd R: For blast-radius caps: propose per-flag max "exposure" = min(tenant_pct, cluster_pct, global_pct). Example: tenant_pct cap = 5%, cluster_pct cap = 10%, global cap = 20%. That way a misclick can't push to 40%.

Maria G: Draft of the auto-rollback rule I'll put in the repo (pseudo):
```
# auto-rollback rule (pseudo)
when (service_error_rate > 0.015 for 3m) or (p95_latency > 1.4*baseline for 5m):
  set_flag("feature_xyz", percentage=0)
  post_incident("rollback_triggered", metadata={"detected_by":"auto-rollback"})
  notify(#eng-oncall, @oncall)
```

Jen S: I'll add that rule to the postmortem action item list and map owners. Quick proposal for deadlines: prototype PR from Maria by Fri, internal canary test by next Tue, blast-radius limiter PR from Zayd by Wed, and rollout guard QA by EOW. Agree?

Alex H: Sounds good. Also add a small migration guard: any flag change > 10% must require two approvals and a dry-run window. We should document that in the rollout playbook.

Maria G: Agree. I'll draft the approval gate + dry-run checklist and link it in the playbook.

Zayd R: One more pattern note from yesterday: the incident had a repeated deploy pattern from the same team pushing quick flag changes. We should add a throttle per-user on flag API (e.g., max N changes per hour) to slow down cascading mistakes. I'll prototype throttling in the flag service.

Jen S: Action items I'll add to tracker (brief):
- Auto-rollback prototype (owner: Maria G) — due: Fri EOD
- Canary test harness + dry-run (owner: Maria G) — due: Tue next week
- Blast-radius limiter (owner: Zayd R) — due: Wed next week
- Approval gate + docs (owner: Alex H / Maria G) — due: Thu next week
- Throttle flag API changes (owner: Zayd R) — due: next sprint start
- Reminders + regression test (owner: Jen S) — in tracker now

IncidentBot: Postmortem doc created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PM-1243 — deadline alignment thread attached.

Alex H: Cool. Let's reconvene after the prototype PR — put a short status update in this thread when you open the PRs. If anyone hits a blocker, ping me and I'll help unblock. :thumbsup:

Maria G: Will do. Opening a PR today for the detection wiring.

Zayd R: Adding the limiter design doc to the design repo by EOD tomorrow.

Jen S: Tracker created and reminders scheduled. I'll ping again in 2 weeks for the 1st follow-up. :calendar:

Alex H: Thanks all. Goal: make sure we never see > 10x blast radius from a single flag mistake again.
